title: Li Bai: Voice of the High Tang Atmosphere
synopsis: The High Tang was an age of romance, poetry, prosperity, and cultural glory. One poet, more than any other, embodies the spirit of this era: Li Bai. Find out about his incredible life in this lesson.

fullText.simplified:
李白——盛唐气象的代言人

    唐人街是海外华人的聚居地，用“唐”字命名，可见唐朝对中国人的影响之深。如果想从一个人身上理解唐朝的气质，非李白莫属。
    李白是唐代著名的浪漫主义诗人。他小时候随家人迁居四川，正赶上唐朝最强盛的时期。这时的唐朝经济繁荣，精神开放，人们乐于吸纳世界各地文化。李白性格乐观大方，喜欢喝酒交朋友。他年轻的时候到处旅游，足迹遍及大半个中国，并结识了许多朋友。这时的他痛饮美酒，随心下笔描绘山川美景。他想象力丰富，看到月亮在江水上的倒影，便写下：“月下飞天镜，云生结海楼”，意思是水中的月亮像一面从天上落下的镜子，江上的云就像一座神奇的楼阁。李白的这种浪漫思想备受唐朝人追捧，让李白成为了文坛新星。
    到了三十岁，李白已经在人才济济的首都很有名了。他和许多人一样，也有梦想：他想入朝做官，做大事。四十三岁时，他终于被当时的皇帝唐玄宗召见。唐玄宗很欣赏他，让他留在身边给自己写诗。这时的李白激动地写下了“仰天大笑出门去，我辈岂是蓬蒿人”，意思是我仰面大笑着走出门去，我怎么会只是一个生活在草野中的平凡人呢？这句诗表现了李白的自信和骄傲，也代表了唐朝开放、自信的精神。
    然而，唐玄宗让李白留在身边，更多的是将他作为宫廷诗人，而非真正的朝臣。他没事就请李白写几首诗赞美一下太平盛世，或者写几首诗夸夸自己最爱的妃子有多漂亮。那时的李白写下了《清平调》赞美杨贵妃，唐玄宗很满意。但这并不是李白的梦想，他厌倦了写诗讨好皇帝的日子。他的性格自由、不受约束，有时喝醉酒后还让皇帝身边的大太监帮他脱鞋，有时甚至拒绝皇帝的召见。最后，唐玄宗给了他一笔钱就让他离开了。
    离开皇宫后，李白像一只飞出笼子的鸟，回到了自由的生活。但他的心情并不完全轻松。他看不惯皇宫里贵族们的生活，觉得他们生活奢侈，不关心百姓的困难。他似乎隐约看到了盛唐即将结束的命运。他的内心充满失望，还好他有一群老朋友们，可以一起喝酒、写诗。他和老朋友们喝酒喝到尽兴时写下了《将进酒》：“天生我材必有用，千金散尽还复来。”意思是上天生下我就有我的用处，即使千两黄金花光了，也可以再赚回来。这首诗先是感叹时间迅速，不知不觉自己头发白了，继而乐观地说出我有自己的价值，再到最后自信地感叹：“优秀的人总是寂寞的，不如在酒中化解悲伤。”这首诗鼓励了后世很多遇到挫折的读者。
    李白一生共写下了900多首诗。作为盛唐文化的象征，李白的诗既有个人的狂放，也有时代的回响，折射出盛唐的繁华，同时隐含着即将到来的政治危机。他的诗将生命的激情与对社会的批判融为一体，吸引着历代读者。
fullText.traditional:
李白——盛唐氣象的代言人

    唐人街是海外華人的聚居地，用“唐”字命名，可見唐朝對中國人的影響之深。如果想從一個人身上理解唐朝的氣質，非李白莫屬。
    李白是唐代著名的浪漫主義詩人。他小時候隨家人遷居四川，正趕上唐朝最強盛的時期。這時的唐朝經濟繁榮，精神開放，人們樂於吸納世界各地文化。李白性格樂觀大方，喜歡喝酒交朋友。他年輕的時候到處旅遊，足跡遍及大半個中國，並結識了許多朋友。這時的他痛飲美酒，隨心下筆描繪山川美景。他想象力豐富，看到月亮在江水上的倒影，便寫下：“月下飛天鏡，雲生結海樓”，意思是水中的月亮像一面從天上落下的鏡子，江上的雲就像一座神奇的樓閣。李白的這種浪漫思想備受唐朝人追捧，讓李白成為了文壇新星。
    到了三十歲，李白已經在人才濟濟的首都很有名了。他和許多人一樣，也有夢想：他想入朝做官，做大事。四十三歲時，他終於被當時的皇帝唐玄宗召見。唐玄宗很欣賞他，讓他留在身邊給自己寫詩。這時的李白激動地寫下了“仰天大笑出門去，我輩豈是蓬蒿人”，意思是我仰面大笑著走出門去，我怎麼會只是一個生活在草野中的平凡人呢？這句詩表現了李白的自信和驕傲，也代表了唐朝開放、自信的精神。
    然而，唐玄宗讓李白留在身邊，更多的是將他作為宮廷詩人，而非真正的朝臣。他沒事就請李白寫幾首詩讚美一下太平盛世，或者寫幾首詩誇誇自己最愛的妃子有多漂亮。那時的李白寫下了《清平調》讚美楊貴妃，唐玄宗很滿意。但這並不是李白的夢想，他厭倦了寫詩討好皇帝的日子。他的性格自由、不受約束，有時喝醉酒後還讓皇帝身邊的大太監幫他脫鞋，有時甚至拒絕皇帝的召見。最後，唐玄宗給了他一筆錢就讓他離開了。
    離開皇宮後，李白像一隻飛出籠子的鳥，回到了自由的生活。但他的心情並不完全輕鬆。他看不慣皇宮裡貴族們的生活，覺得他們生活奢侈，不關心百姓的困難。他似乎隱約看到了盛唐即將結束的命運。他的內心充滿失望，還好他有一群老朋友們，可以一起喝酒、寫詩。他和老朋友們喝酒喝到盡興時寫下了《將進酒》：“天生我材必有用，千金散盡還復來。”意思是上天生下我就有我的用處，即使千兩黃金花光了，也可以再賺回來。這首詩先是感嘆時間迅速，不知不覺自己頭髮白了，繼而樂觀地說出我有自己的價值，再到最後自信地感嘆：“優秀的人總是寂寞的，不如在酒中化解悲傷。”這首詩鼓勵了後世很多遇到挫折的讀者。
    李白一生共寫下了900多首詩。作為盛唐文化的象徵，李白的詩既有個人的狂放，也有時代的迴響，折射出盛唐的繁華，同時隱含著即將到來的政治危機。他的詩將生命的激情與對社會的批判融為一體，吸引著歷代讀者。

sentences.traditional: 有時喝醉酒後還讓皇帝身邊的大太監幫他脫鞋，
sentences.pinyin: yǒu shí hē zuì jiǔ hòu hái ràng huáng dì shēn biān de dà tài jiàn bāng tā tuō xié
sentences.english: His character was liberated and unrestrained.

sentences.simplified: 有时甚至拒绝皇帝的召见。
sentences.traditional: 有時甚至拒絕皇帝的召見。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu shí shèn zhì jù jué huáng dì de zhào jiàn
sentences.english: Sometimes, when drunk, he asked a senior eunuch close to the emperor to take off his shoes.

sentences.simplified: 最后，唐玄宗给了他一笔钱就让他离开了。
sentences.traditional: 最後，唐玄宗給了他一筆錢就讓他離開了。
sentences.pinyin: zuì hòu táng xuán zōng gěi le tā yì bǐ qián jiù ràng tā lí kāi le
sentences.english: At other times, he even refused the emperor’s summons.
In the end, Emperor Xuanzong gave him some money and asked him to leave.

sentences.simplified: 离开皇宫后，李白像一只飞出笼子的鸟，回到了自由的生活。
sentences.traditional: 離開皇宮後，李白像一隻飛出籠子的鳥，回到了自由的生活。
sentences.pinyin: lí kāi huáng gōng hòu lǐ bái xiàng yì zhī fēi chū lóng zi de niǎo huí dào le zì yóu de shēng huó

sentences.simplified: 但他的心情并不完全轻松。他看不惯皇宫里贵族们的生活，
sentences.traditional: 但他的心情並不完全輕鬆。他看不慣皇宮裡貴族們的生活，
sentences.pinyin: dàn tā de xīn qíng bìng bù wán quán qīng sōng tā kàn bu guàn huáng gōng lǐ guì zú men de shēng huó
sentences.english: Leaving the palace, Li Bai was like a little bird leaving its cage, returning to a life of freedom.

sentences.simplified: 觉得他们生活奢侈，不关心百姓的困难。
sentences.traditional: 覺得他們生活奢侈，不關心百姓的困難。
sentences.pinyin: jué de tā men shēng huó shē chǐ bù guān xīn bǎi xìng de kùn nan
sentences.english: However, his mind was not completely at ease. He couldn't stand the lifestyle of the nobles in the palace.

sentences.simplified: 他似乎隐约看到了盛唐即将结束的命运。
sentences.traditional: 他似乎隱約看到了盛唐即將結束的命運。
sentences.pinyin: tā sì hū yǐn yuē kàn dào le shèng táng jí jiāng jié shù de mìng yùn
sentences.english: He thought that they lived extravagantly and did not care about the difficulties of the people.

sentences.simplified: 他的内心充满失望，还好他有一群老朋友们，可以一起喝酒、写诗。
sentences.traditional: 他的內心充滿失望，還好他有一群老朋友們，可以一起喝酒、寫詩。
sentences.pinyin: tā de nèi xīn chōng mǎn shī wàng hái hǎo tā yǒu yì qún lǎo péng you men kě yǐ yì qǐ hē jiǔ xiě shī
sentences.english: It was as if he had hazily glimpsed that the High Tang was soon fated to end.

sentences.simplified: 他和老朋友们喝酒喝到尽兴时写下了《将进酒》：
sentences.traditional: 他和老朋友們喝酒喝到盡興時寫下了《將進酒》：
sentences.pinyin: tā hé lǎo péng you men hē jiǔ hē dào jìn xìng shí xiě xià le qiāng jìn jiǔ
sentences.english: His heart was filled with disappointment, but fortunately he still had his old friends to drink and write poetry with.

sentences.simplified: “天生我材必有用，千金散尽还复来。”
sentences.traditional: “天生我材必有用，千金散盡還復來。”
sentences.pinyin: tiān shēng wǒ cái bì yǒu yòng qiān jīn sàn jìn hái fù lái
sentences.english: When he had drunk to his heart's content with his old friends, he wrote "Bring In the Wine":

sentences.simplified: 意思是上天生下我就有我的用处，即使千两黄金花光了，也可以再赚回来。
sentences.traditional: 意思是上天生下我就有我的用處，即使千兩黃金花光了，也可以再賺回來。
sentences.pinyin: yì si shì shàng tiān shēng xià wǒ jiù yǒu wǒ de yòng chu jí shǐ qiān liǎng huáng jīn huā guāng le yě kě yǐ zài zhuàn huí lai
sentences.english: "Heaven bore my talents, and they must have a purpose. I scatter a thousand taels of gold, and they all come back again."

sentences.simplified: 这首诗先是感叹时间迅速，不知不觉自己头发白了，
sentences.traditional: 這首詩先是感嘆時間迅速，不知不覺自己頭髮白了，
sentences.pinyin: zhè shǒu shī xiān shì gǎn tàn shí jiān xùn sù bù zhī bù jué zì jǐ tóu fa bái le
sentences.english: This means, "Heaven gave birth to me for a reason; even if I spend a thousand taels of gold, I will be able to earn it back."

sentences.simplified: 继而乐观地说出我有自己的价值，再到最后自信地感叹：
sentences.traditional: 繼而樂觀地說出我有自己的價值，再到最後自信地感嘆：
sentences.pinyin: jì ér lè guān de shuō chū wǒ yǒu zì jǐ de jià zhí zài dào zuì hòu zì xìn de gǎn tàn
sentences.english: This poem starts with a sigh at the rapid passage of time, which turned his hair white without him realizing.

sentences.simplified: “优秀的人总是寂寞的，不如在酒中化解悲伤。”
sentences.traditional: “優秀的人總是寂寞的，不如在酒中化解悲傷。”
sentences.pinyin: yōu xiù de rén zǒng shì jì mò de bù rú zài jiǔ zhōng huà jiě bēi shāng
sentences.english: He then continues to optimistically state that he has his own value, before ending with a confident exclamation:

sentences.simplified: 这首诗鼓励了后世很多遇到挫折的读者。
sentences.traditional: 這首詩鼓勵了後世很多遇到挫折的讀者。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shǒu shī gǔ lì le hòu shì hěn duō yù dào cuò zhé de dú zhě
sentences.english: "Exceptional people are always lonely: it's better to drown your sorrows in wine."
This poem has encouraged many readers of later generations who have encountered setbacks.

sentences.simplified: 李白一生共写下了900多首诗。
sentences.traditional: 李白一生共寫下了900多首詩。
sentences.pinyin: lǐ bái yì shēng gòng xiě xià le 2 duō shǒu shī

sentences.simplified: 作为盛唐文化的象征，李白的诗既有个人的狂放，也有时代的回响，
sentences.traditional: 作為盛唐文化的象徵，李白的詩既有個人的狂放，也有時代的迴響，
sentences.pinyin: zuò wéi shèng táng wén huà de xiàng zhēng lǐ bái de shī jì yǒu gè rén de kuáng fàng yě yǒu shí dài de huí xiǎng
sentences.english: Li Bai wrote more than 900 poems in his lifetime.

sentences.simplified: 折射出盛唐的繁华，同时隐含着即将到来的政治危机。
sentences.traditional: 折射出盛唐的繁華，同時隱含著即將到來的政治危機。
sentences.pinyin: zhé shè chū shèng táng de fán huá tóng shí yǐn hán zhe jí jiāng dào lái de zhèng zhì wēi jī
sentences.english: As a symbol of the culture of the High Tang, Li Bai's poetry embodies both unrestrained individual expression and the spirit of the age.

sentences.simplified: 他的诗将生命的激情与对社会的批判融为一体，吸引着历代读者。
sentences.traditional: 他的詩將生命的激情與對社會的批判融為一體，吸引著歷代讀者。
sentences.pinyin: tā de shī jiāng shēng mìng de jī qíng yǔ duì shè huì de pī pàn róng wéi yì tǐ xī yǐn zhe lì dài dú zhě
sentences.english: It reflects the prosperity of the High Tang while also hinting at the impending political crisis.

sentence_translations: Li Bai: Voice of the High Tang Atmosphere
Chinatown (唐人街) refers to a place where overseas Chinese settle.
The use of the character 唐 in its name shows the profound influence of the Tang Dynasty on Chinese people.
If you want to understand the mood of the Tang Dynasty through one person, it has to be Li Bai.
Li Bai was a famous romantic poet of the Tang Dynasty.
When he was a child, he moved with his family to Sichuan, coinciding with the peak of the Tang Dynasty.
This was a time of social and economic prosperity and a liberated cultural atmosphere.
People were happy to absorb cultural influences from all over the world.
LI Bai had an optimistic and easygoing personality and enjoyed drinking and making friends.
In his youth, he traveled extensively over most of China, making many friends along the way.
During this time, he drank fine wine heartily and wrote freely to describe beautiful landscapes.
He had a rich imagination. When he saw the reflection of the moon in a river, he wrote:
"The moon a mirror from Heaven; the clouds rise, forming pavilions in the sky".
This means that the moon in the river is like a mirror fallen from Heaven, and the clouds above the river appear like wondrous pavilions.
This kind of romantic idea was hugely popular with the people of the Tang, making Li Bai a rising star on the literary scene.
By the time he was thirty, Li Bai was already famous in a capital bulging with talent.
Like many other people, he also had dreams: he wanted to be an official at court and do great things.
When he was forty-three, he was finally summoned for an audience by the emperor at the time, Emperor Xuanzong of Tang.
Emperor Xuanzong appreciated Li Bai highly, and kept him by his side to write poetry.
This was the time when Li Bai, filled with passion, wrote:
"Looking up at Heaven, I laugh heartily as I stride out of the door. We are not mere dwellers in the wilderness!"
This means, "I look up and laugh heartily as I walk out of the door; I am no mere commoner, living in the wilderness!"
This line expresses Li Bai’s self-confidence and pride while also expressing the liberated and self-confident spirit of the Tang.
However, Emperor Xuanzong of Tang kept Li Bai by his side more as a court poet than as a true court official.
When he had nothing to do, he would ask Li Bai to write poems in praise of the era of peace and prosperity, ..
.. or to write poems in praise of the beauty of his favorite concubine.
It was during this time that Li Bai wrote "The Quiet, Peaceful Melody" in praise of Noble Consort Yang.
Emperor Xuanzong was very satisfied, but this was not what Li Bai had dreamed of.
He had grown fed up with spending his days writing poetry to flatter the emperor.
His character was liberated and unrestrained.
Sometimes, when drunk, he asked a senior eunuch close to the emperor to take off his shoes.
At other times, he even refused the emperor’s summons.
In the end, Emperor Xuanzong gave him some money and asked him to leave.
Leaving the palace, Li Bai was like a little bird leaving its cage, returning to a life of freedom.
However, his mind was not completely at ease. He couldn't stand the lifestyle of the nobles in the palace.
He thought that they lived extravagantly and did not care about the difficulties of the people.
It was as if he had hazily glimpsed that the High Tang was soon fated to end.
His heart was filled with disappointment, but fortunately he still had his old friends to drink and write poetry with.
When he had drunk to his heart's content with his old friends, he wrote "Bring In the Wine":
"Heaven bore my talents, and they must have a purpose. I scatter a thousand taels of gold, and they all come back again."
This means, "Heaven gave birth to me for a reason; even if I spend a thousand taels of gold, I will be able to earn it back."
This poem starts with a sigh at the rapid passage of time, which turned his hair white without him realizing.
He then continues to optimistically state that he has his own value, before ending with a confident exclamation:
"Exceptional people are always lonely: it's better to drown your sorrows in wine."
This poem has encouraged many readers of later generations who have encountered setbacks.
Li Bai wrote more than 900 poems in his lifetime.
As a symbol of the culture of the High Tang, Li Bai's poetry embodies both unrestrained individual expression and the spirit of the age.
It reflects the prosperity of the High Tang while also hinting at the impending political crisis.
His poetry blends a passion for life with social critique, captivating readers across generations.
